title: Bounded model task boundaries with an unchanged deterministic fallback
request: Implement only TP-02 after reading the planning README, master specification and package prompt; run required checks and independent review, then stop.
plan: Verify TP-01 acceptance and inspect the current adapter, validator, gateway, harness and privacy conventions.
Write failing success and fallback tests before implementing a narrow proposal protocol.
Compile only task groups and dependencies; preserve atomic tasks and run the existing deterministic validator.
Bound provider attempts, tokens, cost and time through the existing gateway; keep its actual API thinking summary.
Measure nine scripted DEV scenarios, run package and repository checks, fix review findings and record the final results.

decisions.decision: Use a separate task_decomposer role through the existing harness and model gateway.
decisions.why: The existing decomposer creates business problem maps and solution_planner changes solution decisions. Neither role owns execution task boundaries.

decisions.decision: Accept only existing task IDs, group membership and prerequisite IDs from the model.
decisions.why: Copying atomic tasks from the freshly checked adapter preserves scientific actions, safety checks, approvals, artifacts and provenance without relying on a model to reproduce them correctly.

decisions.decision: Return the supplied deterministic result unchanged on refusal or unavailability.
decisions.why: A model proposal is optional. Invalid or missing proposals cannot remove the known deterministic plan, and stale or blocked plans remain explicitly unauthorized.

decisions.decision: Add opt-in single-attempt, timeout, full-token and known-price controls to the shared gateway.
decisions.why: One completion could otherwise trigger gateway retries, provider compatibility retries or a shadow request. Existing callers retain their old behavior.

decisions.decision: Keep all product callers and execution defaults unchanged.
decisions.why: This package evaluates proposals only. Task execution, per-task plans and promotion require later packages.

change: Added a proposal-only task decomposer, a versioned prompt, one new harness role and gateway purpose, strict optional request bounds, actual API thinking summary labeling and persistence tests, marked-cell privacy coverage, a scripted DEV comparison and acceptance guide.

findings.defect: The task decomposition API did not exist at the start of the package.
findings.scenario: Importing the new success and exact-fallback tests failed with a missing decomposer module.
findings.cause: TP-01 implemented only deterministic task contracts, validation and adaptation.
findings.fix: Implemented a bounded boundary proposal compiler and a gateway-backed caller, preserving every atomic task.
findings.test: The task decomposer suite exercises accepted proposals, exact fallback and unsafe or stale inputs.

findings.defect: A single gateway completion could make several provider requests and an unbudgeted shadow request.
findings.scenario: A transient failure or provider compatibility refusal retries internally even when the planner makes one completion call.
findings.cause: Existing gateway and transport retry defaults serve conversational callers rather than a one-attempt planner.
findings.fix: Added optional strict controls that disable retries and shadows and reserve known-price input plus full thinking/output limits.
findings.test: Scripted transient failure, shadow routing, Anthropic thinking refusal, unknown price and endpoint token-floor tests all retain the exact fallback.

findings.defect: The first focused run found no data-limit inventory entry for the new purpose.
findings.scenario: The required privacy suite rejected task_decomposer because every purpose must have its own marked-cell test.
findings.cause: The new purpose had dedicated privacy tests but had not joined the repository-wide data-limit inventory.
findings.fix: Added a real captured-request test using marked rows and previews and registered it in the existing inventory.
findings.test: The repaired privacy file passed all 44 tests; the combined task, gateway, transport and thinking suite passed 146 tests.

findings.defect: A direct multi-file unittest run observed shared model environment state and failed existing tests.
findings.scenario: Existing gateway tests received no client after other files changed environment settings in the shared process.
findings.cause: The ad hoc command did not isolate each test file as the repository runner does.
findings.fix: Used the repository's isolated parallel runner and retained the failed command in the acceptance ledger.
findings.test: All 146 tests in the relevant five isolated test files passed.

findings.defect: A current deterministic graph at revision two was falsely refused as stale.
findings.scenario: The adapter produced a revision-two graph, but decomposition silently rebuilt revision one before comparing identities.
findings.cause: The freshness check used the adapter's default revision instead of the supplied graph's revision.
findings.fix: Read and validate the supplied baseline first and recompile the current metadata at that baseline revision.
findings.test: The revision-two regression failed before the fix and passed afterward, producing a revision-three proposal.

findings.defect: An SDK timeout and late-answer check did not bound the whole synchronous planning call.
findings.scenario: The reviewer's sleeping transport returned well after its small planning budget, so fallback could wait indefinitely on a stuck transport.
findings.cause: Network timeouts are not an interrupting whole-call deadline.
findings.fix: Use a restored POSIX main-thread real-time alarm for proposal work and refuse the model before requesting when that facility is unavailable or already in use.
findings.test: An actually sleeping transport is interrupted, worker threads fall back without requesting, and an existing caller alarm and handler remain intact.
findings.open: Model proposals remain a synchronous developer preview. Product worker integration requires an appropriate cancellable host; deterministic fallback works there now.

findings.defect: An interrupting deadline could leak the request's reserved budget during acquisition or handoff.
findings.scenario: A warmed reservation wrapper acquired the project hold and then slept; the deadline returned fallback but left money marked as reserved without a provider call.
findings.cause: The existing release finally began only after reserve returned, so an interruption before ownership transferred could lose the release callback.
findings.fix: Establish context-local cleanup before acquisition, register an idempotent lease before applying holds, and defer alarms only during the tiny in-memory hold/refund updates.
findings.test: The warmed handoff regression failed before the fix. Handoff timeout, slow cap callback and injected alarm during hold mutation now release every hold with no extra provider call.

findings.defect: Masking the main OS thread alone did not make lease bookkeeping safe from a process-directed alarm.
findings.scenario: Another unmasked thread received the real timer signal and Python scheduled the handler on main after the first hold write, before the lease was marked active.
findings.cause: OS signal masks apply per thread, while Python runs the signal handler on main. The original injected-signal regression targeted main only.
findings.fix: Use a Python-level budget critical section recognized by the deadline handler. Mark expiration while bookkeeping is active, complete the tiny transaction, and then raise immediately so the owned lease is refunded.
findings.test: A real timer with another thread and an instrumented hold dictionary failed before this fix and passes afterward without held funds or a provider call.

findings.defect: The workflow training builder did not assign the new model purpose to a stage.
findings.scenario: The broad package gate ran more than four thousand tests and failed the existing every-purpose-has-a-stage inventory for task_decomposer.
findings.cause: The new role was registered with the gateway, harness, prompt and privacy inventory but not the retained-exchange stage map.
findings.fix: Map task_decomposer explicitly to the planning stage and keep the inventory test unchanged.
findings.test: A new regression failed on the missing entry, then verifies the API summary survives record shaping and planning-set construction with recorded provenance.

findings.defect: The scripted runner named three existing standard-tier overrides that lacked concrete configuration documentation.
findings.scenario: After the new runner was staged, the full repository scan found its standard-tier endpoint, model and key names missing from the example environment file.
findings.cause: The existing example documented generic tier overrides and other tiers, but not those three literal standard-tier names. The inventory scans tracked files, so the unstaged runner was absent from the first check.
findings.fix: Document the three optional standard-tier overrides with empty safe defaults and their existing provider inheritance behavior.
findings.test: The unchanged configuration inventory failed in the full run and passed after the documentation fix.

measurements.name: Focused proposal and gateway checks
measurements.gate: Task proposal, gateway compatibility, marked-cell privacy and thinking capture tests must pass without live models.
measurements.result: The initial repaired run passed 146 tests across five isolated files. The final deadline/lease fixes passed 184 tests across seven files, including all 39 task tests. No skips.
limits: Scripted transports and authored metadata do not measure real model plan quality.

measurements.name: Scripted DEV boundary comparison
measurements.gate: All nine declared scenarios must have their expected outcome, preserve structural source coverage and return exact fallback on every refusal.
measurements.result: Nine of nine scenarios passed. Three valid proposals were accepted; three deliberately invalid replies were refused; three incomplete or stale sources blocked before a request. Six exact fallbacks. Six scripted provider calls, zero live calls and zero tasks executed.
limits: One independent binary fixture. The injected invalid proposal rate of three in six is a checker test, not a measured model failure rate.

measurements.name: Prompt and harness evaluation
measurements.gate: The scripted agent suite must record current prompt hashes with no policy errors; all harness regression cases must pass.
measurements.result: Agent evaluation completed with zero errors in all three policies; harness evaluation passed all seventeen cases. Prompt and harness freshness checks passed five tests.

measurements.name: Initial broad package gate
measurements.gate: All selected file tests, evidence checks and product flows must pass before the package is accepted.
measurements.result: 4545 tests across 393 files and 604 units ran in 2278.8 seconds. One stage-map inventory test failed; ten existing skips. All ten evidence/freshness checks and all five product flows passed. PostgreSQL did not start after the file failure.
measurements.next: Register the new purpose's planning stage, prove summary retention and rerun the required final gates.

measurements.name: Final package gates and independent review
measurements.gate: Required package and repository checks must pass and independent review must leave no unresolved correctness findings before completion.
measurements.result: In progress; no completion claim until the final recorded gates and review finish.

outcome: The implementation and scripted DEV checks are complete. Final required gates and independent review are in progress; TP-03 is not started.
lessons: A compiler can preserve immutable scientific tasks while a model proposes useful group boundaries.
Count provider retries and shadows when limiting model calls; one application completion is not necessarily one provider attempt.
Check the effective token limit including thinking headroom and endpoint floors, and fail closed on an unknown price.
Treat scripted adversarial rejection rates as checker evidence, never as real model quality.
risks: The existing adapter supports only basic binary workflows; general branch scheduling and programme decomposition are not proved here.
The interrupting deadline needs a POSIX main-thread caller with no active caller alarm; other contexts use deterministic fallback before requesting a model.
Metadata text must remain free of table values and secrets; the model never receives profiles or rows through this API.
